solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bells ring round parish centre, one nonstop

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone

indicators.note: the centre of a six-letter word is its middle two letters
nonstop here means without its final stop, so the last letter of 'one' goes

explanation.surface: A description of church bells pealing around a parish without pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' wraps the ring word about the parish's centre; 'nonstop' means without its final letter, not continuously.
explanation.definitionFit: A carillon is a set of tuned church bells played from a keyboard.

clue.text: Taxi driver circling King's Cross

indicators.note: circling says the driver goes round the king

parts.note: a cabby drives a cab, a taxi
R, from Rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A cab driver going round King's Cross in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' puts R inside CABBY. King's Cross is a London railway station, so 'Cross' looks like part of a place name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross and crabby are both adjectives for being bad-tempered and irritable.

clue.text: It's hard to find it within artillery lines

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery

indicators.note: within puts the word it inside the artillery and lines

parts.note: RY, railway, gives lines in crosswords

explanation.surface: Something tucked away among artillery lines is hard to locate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' serves the definition while the following 'it' is a letter piece; lines as RY (railway) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A rarity is something uncommon, an item seldom encountered or come across.

clue.text: Flyer's short unaspirated cry

parts.note: short and little both mean small in size

indicators.note: unaspirated means said without the breathy h sound, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a howl is a long loud cry

explanation.surface: A bird's brief cry, uttered without breathing out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unaspirated' drops the H from HOWL, leaving OWL.
explanation.definitionFit: The little owl is a small European bird of prey, so it is a flyer.

clue.text: Mariner's on a day off — this one?

definitions.text: Mariner's on a day off — this one?

indicators.note: off says these letters have gone awry and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor on leave for the day: is this the rank he holds?
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the anagram of MARINERSONADAY. The whole clue also defines: a sailor on an ordinary day off.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinary seaman is the lowest rating of sailor in the navy, a mariner.

clue.text: Fraud involving royal racehorses

indicators.note: involving says the fraud wraps round the royal letter

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick, a fraud
R, from Rex or Regina, stands for royal

explanation.surface: A scam involving horses owned by the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts R inside STING.
explanation.definitionFit: A string is the collective term for the racehorses trained at one stable.

clue.text: Best street guide's a gem

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks
the A-Z is a British book of street maps

explanation.surface: Praise for the finest street map as a real treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: The A-Z is the standard British street atlas of London and other cities.
explanation.definitionFit: Topaz is a precious stone, typically yellow, used in jewellery.

clue.text: Rigid Conservative blocked Maggie's sobriquet briefly

indicators.note: blocked says the Conservative letter sits in the way, inside the nickname
briefly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: Margaret Thatcher was nicknamed the Iron Lady

explanation.surface: A hardline Tory stood in the way of Margaret Thatcher's nickname.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims IRON LADY to IRONLAD; 'blocked' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironclad means strict and inflexible, as in an ironclad rule.

clue.text: Fuel holder, nothing left but a measuring device

indicators.note: left here means left out, so the zero is removed

parts.note: a gasometer is a large tank storing gas
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A fuel tank with nothing left in it, only a gauge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' removes the O (nothing) from GASOMETER.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas meter records how much gas a household uses, so it measures consumption.

clue.text: Opportunity to wind up after failing college boss

indicators.note: after says the opportunity and winding come behind the failing

parts.note: a vice is a fault or failing
a chance is an opportunity

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to roll is to wind, as of a scroll

explanation.surface: A college head gets a chance to wrap things up after a failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ROLL into LLOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice-chancellor is the executive head of a British university.

clue.text: Beer with no heart judged to have a head?

definitions.note: verb phrase standing for an adjective, read as 'to have a head' = to be frothy

indicators.note: with no heart means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
rated means assessed or judged

explanation.surface: A beer lacking substance was assessed as having froth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no heart' takes the L out of ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer with bubbles of gas forced in has a frothy top, a head.

clue.text: Unholy pope identifies himself, clutching ring

indicators.note: clutching says the introduction holds the ring inside it

parts.note: a pope named Pius would introduce himself as I'm Pius
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A pope introducing himself while holding his ring, oddly called unholy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clutching' puts O inside I'M PIUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Impious means lacking reverence for God, irreligious.

clue.text: Nut in car picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as by a microphone, so the sound counts

parts.note: the Volkswagen Beetle is a car

explanation.surface: A nut found inside a car and lifted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' says the car's name is heard, not spelt.
explanation.definitionFit: The betel nut, really the areca seed, is chewed as a stimulant in Asia.

clue.text: Creator of Superman, champion wearing size ten pants

indicators.note: wearing says the champion has the scrambled letters on, inside them
pants is slang for rubbish, so these letters are badly arranged

explanation.surface: Clark Kent's creator, or a champion, in size ten underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' rearranges the letters of 'size ten' into NIETZSE; 'wearing' means the champion sits inside them. Superman here is the philosopher's Ubermensch, not the comic hero.
explanation.definitionFit: The philosopher described the Ubermensch, usually translated as Superman, in Thus Spoke Zarathustra.

clue.text: Press university to enter for the country

indicators.note: to enter says the university letter goes into the two words 'for the'

parts.note: a state is a country

explanation.surface: An urging that a university should enlist for national service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts U into FORTHE, after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth estate is a traditional name for journalists and newspapers as a political force.

clue.text: Birches raised in small wood for English person

indicators.note: in puts the raised canes inside the other pieces

parts.note: ash is a wood

indicators.note: raised, in a down clue, means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: birches and canes are both rods used for beating

explanation.surface: Birch trees grown in a little copse, for an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: Birches are the rods once used for punishment, not trees; 'raised' turns the canes into SENAC in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassenach is a Scots term, often derogatory, for an English person.

clue.text: Fife's top resort, where snow's deeper

definitions.note: phrase standing for an adjective or adverb: away from groomed runs

indicators.note: resort, read as re-sort, says these letters are sorted again

explanation.surface: Scotland's best ski resort, in Fife, has the deepest snow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday spot but means re-sort the letters of FIFESTOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-piste skiing is away from prepared runs, in ungroomed and often deeper snow.

clue.text: A pat on the back or a touch on the shoulder?

definitions.meaning: praise or award, a token of approval
the tap of a sword on the shoulder when someone is knighted

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the ceremony of conferring knighthood with a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an honour or praise and the ceremonial sword tap at knighting.

clue.text: Incompetence not a trait of Mrs Brown's Boys?

definitions.text: not a trait of Mrs Brown's Boys?
definitions.meaning: read as ..., the lack of the swear word feck, which the show uses constantly

explanation.surface: Is uselessness something the sitcom characters lack?
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Brown's Boys is an Irish TV sitcom whose lead constantly says 'feck', a mild Irish swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: Feckless describes someone ineffective and irresponsible; the noun names that quality.

clue.text: Song and dance promotion

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
an ad is an advertisement, a promotion

explanation.surface: A song-and-dance routine used as publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song and dance' reads as one idiom for a fuss, but 'Song' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a narrative song or slow sentimental song.

clue.text: Get angry about men beginning to thump spinner

indicators.note: about says the anger word goes round the others

parts.note: to vex is to anger; read as get angry, a stretched sense
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers, men

indicators.note: beginning to says take only the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone losing their temper when men start hitting a spin bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: A spinner is a slow bowler in cricket, which the surface suggests; here it is anything that whirls. OR (other ranks) for men is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A vortex is a whirling mass of air or water, something that spins.

clue.text: Eccentric posh priest loathing salt

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: hate is loathing

explanation.surface: An odd upper-class clergyman who detests salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' turns POSH into PHOS.
explanation.definitionFit: A phosphate is a chemical salt of phosphoric acid.

clue.text: Unnamed royal scion's quotation

indicators.note: unnamed means losing N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: a prince is a king's son, a royal offspring

explanation.surface: An anonymous member of the royal family is quoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unnamed' removes N (name) from PRINCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A quotation is a stated cost, as in a builder's quote.

clue.text: She inspires poetry moderator to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says only part of the word 'moderator' is used

explanation.surface: A female muse who partly inspires a chairperson's verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to some extent' points to the letters inside 'moderator'.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek muse of lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: Endurance's mainmast shattered, all except top

indicators.note: shattered means broken up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
all except top means every letter but the first is kept

explanation.surface: Shackleton's ship Endurance with its main mast smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all except top' drops the first M; 'shattered' rearranges AINMAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is the staying power to keep going, physical or mental.

clue.text: Tract that appears in spring

definitions.meaning: a pamphlet or short printed handout
a small young leaf, sprouting in spring

explanation.surface: A pamphlet that comes out every spring.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the word as a little leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a printed handout and a small young leaf.

clue.text: Team takes part in gospel evening

indicators.note: takes part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A team joins in an evening of gospel singing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket or football side has that many players, so the number names a team.

clue.text: Conformist Dorothy endlessly trained to slice beef

indicators.note: to slice says the scrambled letters cut into the beef word

parts.note: beef comes from cattle; an ox is a beef animal

indicators.note: trained means taught a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
endlessly means the last letter of the name is dropped

explanation.surface: Dorothy, endlessly coached, learns to carve beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the name's last letter; 'trained' rearranges the rest to RTHODO, which 'to slice' puts inside the beef animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthodox means following accepted beliefs and conventions, the opposite of a rebel.
